claim_under_test: The LoRa receiver's sample_clk, taken from util_ad9361_divclk/clk_out, is the 62.5 MHz the design is written and constrained for.
result: Refuted. The divider output equals the AD9361 sample rate exactly, at every rate, so the receiver had one fabric clock per sample rather than the sixty-three its joint-search budget assumes.

method.instrument: ADI clock monitor inside axi_ad9361 (up_clock_mon), read over /dev/mem
method.monitored_net: axi_ad9361/clk, which is l_clk and also the input of util_ad9361_divclk

divider.note: BUFGMUX_CTRL selects I0 when S is 0, and I0 is the SEL_0_DIV leg.

consequences.abort_cause: The window ages out at 55552 samples, which is reached long before the 135443 the search needs, so the abort is always the age-out rather than a completed search.

corroboration: Abort lands 55552 samples after the phase-corrected origin with zero residual across five captures.
Fine skip appears 50 to 51 symbols after the coarse resync in all five traces.
toa_search_busy held 60 ms against 55.5 ms predicted, polled at 13.8 ms granularity.

supersedes.claim: The fabric clock is 1.9 to 3.2 MHz.
supersedes.why_it_was_wrong: It divided the simulated search cost by the measured busy duration, which assumes the search runs to completion. It does not; the busy duration measures the age-out instead, so the quotient measured nothing.
